description: Music (via cross-arts) Foundation width tiers — ACARA v9. Foundation descriptors are cross-arts; music is one form among several. Width axis is task_contexts throughout.
subject: Music

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest single arts context that honestly satisfies the descriptor's command term — typically one guided activity in one arts form.
width_notes.typical_width: Engagement across at least two arts forms or activity types, grounded in the most common elaboration cases. Reflects a well-taught Foundation class.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions that add contexts, forms or purposes — not harder versions of the same activity. First Nations contexts included where elaborations indicate them.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations used as source data. Foundation descriptors are cross-arts; elaborations reference Dance, Drama, Media Arts, Music and Visual Arts throughout. Music-specific examples (songs, chants, soundscapes) prioritised in width framing.

AC9AMUFC01.minimum_width: Create a simple arts work in one form (e.g. a composed chant, a drawn scene, or a dramatic play sequence) that communicates an idea from personal experience.
AC9AMUFC01.typical_width: Create arts works across two or more forms that communicate ideas from lived personal or social experiences — e.g. a song or chant combined with movement, or dramatic play with a recorded voice-over; extend and vary known songs, chants or rhymes by changing words, adding movements, or improvising rhythmic accompaniments.
wider: Use available digital devices to compose, record and share a chant or rap that communicates a health, sustainability or process message — combining voice, body percussion and digital capture
Create a multi-form work combining music (chant/soundscape) with visual images or puppetry to retell a familiar story, making decisions about how music and image work together
Devise works using repurposed everyday objects as starting points — explore how materials inspire imagined scenarios and musical/sound decisions
Learn and extend a culturally significant song, chant or musical game using accredited First Nations Australian resources or with guidance from community representatives
elaborations: creating arts works in a range of forms to communicate ideas from lived personal or social experiences; for example, composing a song or chant about a favourite food or activity
creating works in response to inspiration from sources such as play, imagination, observation, literature, artworks from their cultures and communities
extending and varying known songs, chants or rhymes; for example, changing words, interpreting without using voice, adding movements/actions or improvising rhythm patterns as accompaniment
manipulating objects, puppets, 2D images and/or available technologies to create or retell stories
devising a chant/rap to communicate a health or sustainability message; recording using an available digital device
repurposing materials and objects as starting points for imagining and developing scenes and scenarios

AC9AMUFD01.minimum_width: Use play and imagination to explore one arts skill or process (e.g. experimenting with voice to create different sounds, or using movement to respond to music); describe one thing discovered.
AC9AMUFD01.typical_width: Use play, imagination and guided skill-development to discover possibilities across at least two arts contexts — e.g. exploring voice qualities and movement simultaneously, improvising rhythmic patterns and interpreting them visually, or responding to music through movement and image-making.
wider: Explore how tactile qualities of materials (rough, smooth, spikey) can be translated into voice, body movement and sound — connecting material play to musical decision-making
Improvise rhythmic clapping or stamping patterns and represent them visually using shapes, lines and colours — bridging music and visual arts thinking
Take on the point of view of a fictional character using dramatic play, singing voice and movement together — integrating skills across Music, Drama and Dance
Use a camera or digital device to document a creative process through an image sequence, then add voice narration or composed sound as commentary
elaborations: playing with the tactile qualities of a range of materials and exploring how they feel to develop ideas for a soundscape or visual artwork
playing games to develop subject-specific practices such as pitch, beat and/or rhythm recognition
responding to the emotions they experience while listening to different pieces of music and using movement to share their response
improvising rhythmic patterns for clapping or stamping and interpreting these visually using elements of art/design such as shapes, lines and/or colours
exploring their speaking and singing voices and discovering ways they can use their voices/vocalisation to communicate ideas and feelings
improvising movements to explain the steps in a process, then using a camera to capture a series of images or a photographic story

AC9AMUFE01.minimum_width: Identify one way that an arts work (e.g. a song, dance or drawing) is important to people or a community; share a personal response to it.
AC9AMUFE01.typical_width: Explore how facial expressions, gestures, movement and voice communicate emotions in arts works; identify arts works and experiences in their own life (songs, dances, games, animations); listen to First Nations Australians talking about the importance of arts for connecting to People, Culture and Country/Place.
wider: Learn social or cultural dances or songs that have meaning for specific communities, observing relevant protocols and using accredited resources or community representatives
Explore how music is used in celebrations the students know (school songs, birthday songs, sporting anthems) and compare how different communities use music for similar purposes
Investigate how illustrations and music in a shared picture book work together to communicate mood, character or narrative — responding to both visual and aural elements
elaborations: exploring how facial expressions, gestures and other ways of moving, and using voice or language, can communicate emotions and feelings in arts works
identifying and/or learning social or cultural dances that have meaning for people and communities, taking care to observe relevant protocols
identifying arts works and experiences in their lives, such as songs they sing, dances or drama they watch or perform, animations, computer games or music videos
singing songs that are used for celebrations, such as school songs, anthems, sports teams' songs, birthday songs
listening to First Nations Australians talk about the importance of the arts for connecting to People, Culture and Country/Place

AC9AMUFP01.minimum_width: Share a simple arts work with an audience of peers or teacher; introduce it by naming one feature of the work.
AC9AMUFP01.typical_width: Share arts works in multiple formats — e.g. a gallery walk, a performance of a song or soundscape, and a digital image sequence documenting a creative process; talk about ideas, materials or processes used and respond to audience questions.
wider: Use digital devices to record arts explorations and curate a sequence of images showing steps in a creative process, adding voice commentary that expresses feelings and decisions
Perform a musical sequence for other groups, introducing the work by describing favourite moments or explaining choices made
Present a retelling of a story using dramatic play with puppets, repurposed objects or toys — combining movement, voice and musical elements for an audience
elaborations: sharing their artworks with the class via a 'gallery' or 'performance walk'
performing songs, soundscapes or chants/raps, using music skills they have learnt and practised
taking images of class arts events, creating an image sequence to document the occasion, and adding sound
talking about ideas such as themes, processes used to make the work, or features of the work
presenting retellings of stories to peers through dramatic play using repurposed objects, toys or puppets
using digital devices to record their arts explorations; curating a sequence of digital images to show the steps in a process
